title: Adult social care sponsorship: who can switch inside the UK?
summary: Check the care worker and senior care worker rules before taking a job or planning a visa switch. This guide covers occupation codes 6135 and 6136, employers, pay and family restrictions.
content:
# Adult social care sponsorship: who can switch inside the UK?

Last updated: 2026-11-27

## Overseas applications and in-country switching
Since 22 July 2025, these two codes cannot be used for new applications from outside the UK. The Rules still allow some in-country applications. This restriction is about these specific roles, including under ordinary Skilled Worker sponsorship. It does not close all healthcare roles; see [healthcare and NHS roles](/en/work-visa/health-and-care-worker-visa). [Care occupation rules](#guide-evidence-start)

## Check which in-country provision applies
Under SW 6.1B(a), you must have worked lawfully for the employer that will sponsor you in code 6135 or 6136 for at least the three months ending on the date it issues your CoS. You must apply before 22 July 2028. Check the work allowed by your current permission and the separate switching requirements. For example, two months with a different agency and one month with the sponsor do not meet this rule. Ask who actually employed and paid you; working at the same care home is not enough. Under SW 6.1B(b), there is a separate provision for someone with Skilled Worker permission currently sponsored in 6135 or 6136, including legacy codes 6145 and 6146. The three-month condition and the July 2028 deadline are in (a), not (b). If your leave or work history is unclear, get regulated advice before applying. [Switching rules](#guide-evidence-clock)

## Check the sponsor, service and actual pay
Verify the legal employer on the sponsor register and ask who will issue the CoS. If any working location is in England, the sponsor is normally required to hold Care Quality Commission (CQC) registration and currently carry on a regulated activity. Check the provider in the CQC directory. The narrow SW 6.1C exception applies to qualifying workers with continuous care-role Skilled Worker permission dating from rules in force before 11 March 2024 who are continuing with their most recent sponsor. CQC is England’s regulator. Confirm arrangements for the nation where you would work. Under current Health and Care visa sponsorship guidance for these care roles, basic pay must be at least £25,000 a year and at least £12.82 per hour. Check both against the contracted hours and current table. Ask about travel time, rota, location and deductions before accepting work. [Employer and pay rules](#guide-evidence-employer)

## Check each dependant before switching
New switchers into these care codes generally cannot sponsor a dependant partner. Check the exception for workers first granted Skilled Worker permission under the rules in force before 11 March 2024 in code 6145 or 6146 who have since held continuous permission in the qualifying care codes. A child may qualify in specific cases, including UK birth, or certain in-country applications where the sponsored parent is the sole surviving parent, has sole responsibility, or shares responsibility with another qualifying sponsored worker. The child must meet the other requirements. Ask for regulated advice before assuming your family can switch with you. [Dependant rules](#guide-evidence-family)

## Do not pay for a job or CoS
Verify the vacancy with the employer through independently found contact details. A CoS is an electronic reference assigned by the sponsor. Do not pay someone to issue or sell one. Sponsors cannot pass on the applicable CoS fee. Recruitment agencies generally cannot charge for finding you work. Keep the job advert, written offer, contract and lawful work records. Report suspicious offers to the authorities. If you cannot meet the timing before your permission expires, a verbal offer or a pending CoS will not extend it. Check lawful alternatives early or leave by the expiry date if you have no other lawful basis to stay. See [options after graduation](/en/work-visa/uk-options-after-graduation). [Fees, scams and advice](#guide-evidence-safety)
